title: Srinivasa Ramanujan
passages: Srinivasa Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887 in Erode, a town in southern India, and grew up in Kumbakonam, a place famous for its tall, colorful temples. His family spoke Tamil and had little money. At about 15, he borrowed a book listing nearly 5,000 THEOREMS, and he began working through them on his own, filling NOTEBOOKS with bold new ideas. He loved numbers so much that he failed his other college subjects. Later, he took a job as a clerk at the Madras Port Trust and did math in every spare moment.

In 1913, Ramanujan mailed a letter to G. H. Hardy, a famous mathematician at Cambridge, packed with about 120 results. Hardy was amazed. In 1914, Ramanujan sailed to England, a cold, gray land far from home, where he kept to his VEGETARIAN diet even when food was scarce during the war. With Hardy, he studied PARTITIONS, the many ways a number can be split into smaller numbers. In 1918, he became one of the youngest Fellows of the Royal Society. Weakened by illness, he returned to India and died on 26 April 1920, aged just 32.
